definition: The drawing of a sound's amplitude over time.
A picture of how a sound's frequency content changes over time: time across, frequency up, level as colour.
A frequency scale spaced as pitch is heard: roughly linear below 1 kHz and logarithmic above.
note: Duden spelling with hyphen; unit 'mel'.

definition: The moving line that marks the current playback position.
note: Logic Pro de defines it exactly so: 'Die Abspielposition ist die vertikale Linie, die die aktuelle Wiedergabeposition in einem Projekt zeigt.' Not 'Cursor' (Cubase's 'Projekt-Cursor'), so it stays distinct from the Einfügemarke (edit cursor). Use 'Abspielpositionslinie' where the line must be told apart from the time value. The app name Playhead stays English.

definition: The position where editing and playback start, set by clicking.
note: As in Ableton Live de ('Einfügemarke', the blinking insert marker from which playback starts). 'Cursor' is acceptable here but never for the playhead.

definition: Samples per second of a digital sound, in Hz.
note: 'Abtastrate' in standards, textbooks and Audacity de; Cubase de and studio speech often say 'Samplerate'.

definition: Bits per sample of a digital sound; sets its resolution.
note: 'Wortbreite' is the older engineering term.

definition: One signal of a sound file; stereo has two.
One channel.
Two channels, left and right.
Stereo written as the sum (mid) and the difference (side) of the channels.
note: German recording practice: MS-Verfahren, Mitten- und Seitensignal; DAW plug-ins often keep 'Mid/Side'.

definition: Where in its cycle a wave is at a given moment.
Whether a signal is upright or inverted.
note: German studio speech often says 'Phase drehen' for a plain inversion; keep 'Polarität umkehren' for that, as the English does.

definition: How strong a signal is, usually in dB.
note: Pegel ≠ Lautheit. Avoid colloquial 'Lautstärke', which is used for both.

definition: A change of level, in dB.
note: Studio and DAW usage (Cubase, Logic). 'Verstärkung' (Audacity de) suggests only boosting, while a gain can be negative. Gender varies: das Gain / der Gain.

definition: The largest absolute sample value.
note: German broadcast documents contrast 'Sample Peak' with 'True Peak' (ZDF Vorgaben 2022); meters label it 'Peak'. Use 'Spitzenpegel' for the value in dBFS. For a compact meter label 'Peak' is fine next to 'True Peak'.

definition: The peak of the signal between samples, as a DAC would reproduce it.
note: German broadcast usage keeps the English: ZDF Vorgaben 2022 'maximaler Spitzenpegel („Maximum True Peak Level“)', unit dBTP. Hyphenate in compounds: True-Peak-Pegel, True-Peak-Limiter.

definition: How loud a sound is heard, as opposed to its level.
note: DIN 45631 / ISO 532-1; EBU R 128 in German practice ('Programmlautheit', 'Lautheitsbereich'). Not 'Lautstärke'; 'Lautstärkepegel' (phon) is a different quantity.

definition: Loudness units relative to full scale (ITU-R BS.1770); 1 LU is 1 dB.
note: ZDF Vorgaben 2022: 'Absolute Maßeinheit der Lautheit bezogen auf die digitale Vollaussteuerung'. Unit unchanged.

definition: The frequency weighting that loudness meters apply before measuring.
note: ZDF Vorgaben 2022: 'K-Bewertungskurve nach ITU-R BS. 1770'; analogous to A-Bewertung.

definition: Set a sound's peak or loudness to a target.
note: Command 'Normalisieren' (Audacity, Cubase); noun 'Normalisierung'.

definition: A gradual change of level at the start (fade-in) or end (fade-out).
note: Studio and DAW usage (Ableton de 'Fades', Cubase/Logic 'Fade-In/Fade-Out'; Duden spells 'Fade-in/Fade-out'). Broadcast and Audacity de use 'Einblenden/Ausblenden', which also work well as command names.

definition: Distortion when a signal exceeds the largest value that can be stored.
note: 'Übersteuerung' is broader (also analogue, also without hard limiting); for the quality-check finding use 'Clipping'.

definition: A constant shift of the signal away from zero.
note: Studio usage 'DC-Offset'; Audacity de uses 'Gleichspannungsversatz'; textbooks 'Gleichanteil'.

definition: The level of the background noise under a sound.
note: 'Rauschpegel' when the number is meant; 'Rauschteppich' is studio jargon.

definition: A stretch with no sound above the noise floor.
A sound that ends before its decay has died away.
note: Follows tail = Ausklang. Studio speech says 'der Hall reißt ab', hence 'abgerissenes Ende'. The short label reads as a quality-check finding.

definition: One recorded or rendered version of a sound.
note: Studio and DAW usage (Cubase, Logic, Ableton 'Take-Lanes'). Duden: der oder das Take.

definition: Compute a processed sound and write it as audio.
note: Cubase de 'Rendern' (In-Place-Rendering); Logic de 'Bouncen'.

definition: A sound that repeats without an audible join.
note: DAW and sound-design usage (Ableton de 'Loop-Klammer'); 'Schleife' (Audacity de) sounds dated in this context. Duden: der Loop.

definition: A fade-out of one sound overlapping a fade-in of another.
note: Cubase and Ableton de keep 'Crossfade'; broadcast says 'Überblendung' or 'Kreuzblende'.

definition: Cut a sound into parts at chosen points.
note: German DAW and sampler usage keeps 'slicen' (verb) and 'Slice' (the part). 'Zerteilen' is a plain German command if a loan-free UI is wanted.

definition: Change a sound's duration without changing its pitch.
note: Studio usage. 'Zeitdehnung' literally covers only lengthening (shortening would be 'Zeitstauchung'). Paired with Pitch-Shifting.

definition: Change a sound's pitch without changing its duration.
note: Cubase de names the offline process 'Tonhöhenverschiebung'; studio speech says 'Pitch-Shifting' or 'pitchen'. Kept as a loan to pair with Time-Stretching.

definition: The unit of loudness as heard; 1 sone is the loudness of a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL.
note: Unit symbol 'sone' unchanged; noun das Sone, pl. Sone (DIN 45631, Zwicker/Fastl).

definition: How much a sound's energy sits at high frequencies, as heard; in acum.
note: DIN 45692 'Messtechnische Simulation der Hörempfindung Schärfe'; the concept comes from German psychoacoustics (von Bismarck, Aures, Zwicker). Not the same as Härte (harshness).

definition: The rasping quality of fast amplitude modulation (about 15–300 Hz); in asper.
note: Zwicker/Fastl's German texts spell 'Rauhigkeit' (pre-1996 spelling); current spelling 'Rauigkeit', occasionally 'Rauheit'. Distinct from Härte (harshness) and Schärfe (sharpness).

definition: The sensation of slow amplitude modulation (about 1–20 Hz, strongest near 4 Hz); in vacil.
note: Zwicker/Fastl.

definition: Zwicker's combination of loudness, sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength into one annoyance value.
note: Widmann/Zwicker; Fastl and Zwicker 2007. Because 'Lästigkeit' is taken here, it is not used for harshness.

definition: One sound making another harder or impossible to hear.
note: Zwicker/Fastl and German psychoacoustics: Verdeckung, Mithörschwelle; studio and codec literature also say 'Maskierung'.

definition: The frequency range the ear integrates as one; on the Bark scale.
note: Zwicker's German term (Frequenzgruppe, Tonheit in Bark); 'kritisches Band' is a back-translation from English.

definition: A value drawn over time along the waveform.
A small picture of a whole sound used to find one's way in it.
The overview of one sound as Playhead draws it: waveform, curves and marks in one band.
note: 'Streifen' is literal, visual and collides with no DAW term; avoid 'Spur' (= track) and plain 'Band' (frequency band). 'Leiste' reads like a toolbar. A Lane is part of a Streifen.

definition: A named way to draw a strip, written as a short code of layers.
note: 'Look' is an established German loan (Duden; film and photo grading) and stays unambiguous as a named, coded object; 'Darstellung' and 'Ansicht' are already used in UIs for generic display options and zoom/scroll views. Not 'Skin', not 'Design/Theme' (colours only).

definition: The short text that defines a look, for example "form:overlay,shape:mirror,lane:harshness".
note: Follows the choice for 'look' ('Darstellungscode' if 'Darstellung' is chosen). The code keywords stay English because they are syntax.

definition: One element of a look: a waveform, spectrogram, curve, set of marks or sections.
note: 'Ebene' as in German graphics software (Photoshop, GIMP). This deliberately separates drawing layers from the sound layers of the layer-remix tool, for which the sound-design loan 'Layer' is used.

definition: A horizontal band of a strip that holds one curve.
note: As in German DAWs (Ableton de 'Take-Lanes', 'Automations-Lane'; Cubase de 'Lanes'). Avoid 'Spur' (= track). 'Bahn' is the German option for a loan-free UI.

definition: Curves drawn in one shared band instead of separate lanes.
note: Option value next to 'gespiegelt' and 'von der Grundlinie'. Not 'überblendet' (= crossfaded).

definition: Drawn symmetrically above and below a centre line, like a waveform.
note: Kept distinct from 'überlagert' (overlaid).

definition: Drawn upwards from the bottom of the band.
note: Grundlinie = bottom edge of the band, not the waveform's zero line (that is the Mittellinie).

definition: A compact chart that folds a curve into coloured bands of increasing intensity.
note: German visualisation writing mostly keeps the English (also 'Horizon Graph', Heer et al. 2009); 'Horizontdiagramm' is understandable but rarely attested.

definition: A waveform whose height follows a curve, for example perceived loudness, instead of the peak level.
note: 'modellieren' also means shaping by hand (clay), so it carries 'sculpted'; 'geformt' is neutral but bland; 'skulptiert' is not idiomatic German.

definition: The ordinary peak waveform drawn as a thin line behind another layer.
Ticks along the strip at events, onsets, beats or section boundaries.
note: Not 'Marker': in DAWs those are user-set position markers.

definition: The text that says what each colour and line of a strip shows.
How much Playhead analyses: fast (curves only), sound effect, or music.
A number or curve computed from a sound that describes one of its properties.
note: Peeters et al. 2011 (Timbre Toolbox).

definition: A descriptor used as input to a classifier or search.
note: German pattern-recognition usage: Merkmal, Merkmalsextraktion, Merkmalsvektor; MIR jargon also says 'Feature'. Keeps feature ≠ descriptor.

definition: How much is happening: spectral change and the density of events.
note: Literal, immediately clear and short. 'Bewegtheit' is a musicological term with a similar meaning but less suited to a UI label. Not 'Aktivierung' (psychology, close to arousal).

definition: How exciting or calming a sound is, after the psychological dimension of the same name.
note: German emotion psychology uses both 'Erregung' and the loan 'Arousal' (valence/arousal after Russell). Not 'Aktivierung' (collides with Aktivität) and not 'Anregung' (= excitation in cross-synthesis).

definition: How unpleasant a sound is to listen to, computed from psychoacoustic annoyance; not the same as roughness.
note: 'Härte' is studio jargon ('Härten in den Hochmitten'), short, and clearly separate from Schärfe and Rauigkeit; risk: confusion with material or mallet hardness in the impact model, so write those as compounds ('Schlägelhärte'). 'Harschheit' is unambiguous but rare; 'Lästigkeit' is taken by psychoacoustic annoyance.

definition: Build-up and release over time, after the model of musical tension by Farbood (2012).
note: Established in musicology (Spannung und Entspannung/Lösung). In technical prose 'Spannung' can be read as electrical voltage; write 'musikalische Spannung' where needed.

definition: How far the harmony is from rest, from the tonal interval space.
note: Bernardes et al. 2016 (Tonal Interval Space, TIV).

definition: How much a moment differs from what came before.
note: Foote 2000. German MIR writing (e.g. AudioLabs Erlangen) mostly keeps 'Novelty-Kurve' in English. Keep distinct from 'spektrale Überraschung' and 'Informationsgehalt' (surprisal).

definition: Change of the spectrum that loudness does not explain.
note: Literal and clear; stays apart from 'Neuheit' (which also includes level changes) and from 'Informationsgehalt' (surprisal). Never shorten to bare 'Überraschung', or the line to surprisal blurs.

definition: Information content of an event: the less expected, the higher.
note: Standard German information-theory term (Shannon: Informationsgehalt, Selbstinformation); music cognition and psycholinguistics also use the loan 'Surprisal'. 'Überraschungswert' avoided so it cannot be confused with spectral surprise.

definition: Where a piece moves to a new part, signed: up where sound enters, down where it falls away or breaks off.
note: 'Strukturwechsel' is short and neutral (works for SFX as well as music); 'Formwechsel' is more musicological; 'strukturelle Änderung' is literal but long. Signed labels in the UI: 'oben: Einsatz, unten: Wegfall oder Abbruch'.

definition: How clearly a regular pulse is felt at each moment.
note: Grosche and Müller 2011 (predominant local pulse, PLP). Not 'Beat-Stärke'.

definition: The moment a sound or note begins.
note: German MIR and DSP usage keeps 'Onset' (Onset-Detektion); musicians say '(Ton-)Einsatz'. Onset (instant) ≠ Attack (phase up to the peak) ≠ Transiente (fast change).

definition: How strongly new sound arrives at each moment; peaks are hits.
One distinct sound within a file, such as a hit, a step or a creak, with a start and an end.
note: Not 'Event': in Cubase an Event is a clip on a track.

definition: The first part of a sound, from its start to its peak.
note: Synth and studio usage; acoustics says 'Einschwingphase/Einschwingvorgang', percussion 'Anschlag'. Gender varies (der/die Attack); plural Attacks.

definition: The sustained, often tonal, part of a sound after its attack.
note: Studio jargon ('der Snare fehlt Körper'); 'Body' is also common. Not 'Klangkörper' (= instrument body or orchestra) and not 'Sustain' (an ADSR level).

definition: The part of a sound in which it dies away.
note: Do not equate with the Decay stage of an ADSR envelope (fall to the sustain level), where German synths keep 'Decay'. Acoustics: Ausschwingvorgang.

definition: The late part of a decay, including reverberation.
note: Studio jargon 'Fahne' (Hallfahne); 'Ausklang' is understood by everyone and forms good tool names (Ausklänge verbreitern). Plural Ausklänge.

definition: A short, fast change of level and spectrum, typically at an attack.
note: Plural 'Transienten' (Ableton de, studio). Gender varies: die Transiente / der Transient.

definition: The regular pulse a listener taps along to.
note: Ableton de writes both 'Beats' and 'Schlägen'; music theory says Schlag, Grundschlag, Zählzeit.

definition: The first beat of a bar.
note: Musicians say 'die Eins'; German MIR writing keeps 'Downbeat'.

definition: A group of beats, usually four.
note: US 'measure' is also 'Takt'. Not to be confused with bar-shape (Stab).

definition: The speed of the beat, in beats per minute (BPM).
A part of a piece, such as an intro or chorus, found from where its sound changes.
note: 'Formteil' is the musicological term for music; 'Abschnitt' also fits sound effects.

definition: How much a sound returns to states it has been in before.
note: Marwan et al. 2007; German: Rekurrenzplot, Rekurrenzquantifizierungsanalyse.

definition: How often a pattern repeats, in Hz.
How strongly a sound is periodic (pitched) rather than noisy.
note: Hillenbrand et al. 1994.

definition: How steadily a sound's phases advance; 1 for a steady tone, near 0 for noise.
How much a sound changes when played backwards; high for hits that decay.
note: 'Zeitpfeil' is the established German physics term for the arrow of time and short; 'Zeitasymmetrie' is more technical. For docs: zeitliche Irreversibilität (Ramsey and Rothman 1996).

definition: How much a sound consists of clicks, cracks and crackle, from spectral kurtosis.
note: 'Impulshaltigkeit' is the established term of German noise assessment (DIN 45645-1, TA Lärm: 'impulshaltige Geräusche') and fits the meaning, although there it is rated from level differences, not spectral kurtosis. 'Impulsivität' sounds like a character trait. Not 'Spitzigkeit' (spikiness).

definition: A statistic that is 0 for steady noise, −1 for a steady tone and large for clicks.
note: Antoni 2006; German machine-diagnostics literature mostly says 'spektrale Kurtosis'.

definition: How fast the spectrum's centre moves up or down, in octaves per second.
note: Literal and clear; 'Schwerpunktbewegung' is more precise (it is the centroid that moves) but unclear without context; 'Drift' suggests slow change.

definition: The centre of mass of a spectrum; a measure of brightness.
Spectral change that does not move the centre, as when a spectrum spreads or narrows.
note: 'Umformung' is short and sits well next to 'spektrale Bewegung'; 'spektrale Umformung' is clearer in docs.

definition: Whether events come regularly (below 0), at random (0) or in bursts (above 0).
note: Goh and Barabási 2008; German scientific writing leaves it untranslated. If a German UI word is wanted, descriptive 'Schubhaftigkeit' or 'Häufung' could serve, but neither is established.

definition: How evenly a sound's energy is spread over time.
note: Sueur et al. 2008 (Ht).

definition: The time a sound takes to fall by 60 dB.
note: In room acoustics T60 is the 'Nachhallzeit' (DIN EN ISO 3382); for sounds and struck objects in general 'Abklingzeit'.

definition: How quickly a vibrating body loses energy.
What an impacted object is made of, as heard: damped, glass-like or metal-like.
note: Klatzky et al. 2000.

definition: One frequency component of a sound.
A partial above the lowest one.
note: Counting: 1. Oberton = 2. Teilton.

definition: With partials that are not whole-number multiples of a fundamental, as in bells and struck metal.
note: German instrument acoustics also writes 'unharmonische Teiltöne'.

definition: Automatic checks for clipping, DC offset, silence and cut tails.
A test that edits a sound in a known way and checks that the analysis changes as it must.
note: 'Selbsttest' is familiar (device self-test) and short; 'Plausibilitätstest' describes the purpose but sounds bureaucratic. Not 'Unit-Test/Modultest'. Method: metamorphes Testen (Chen et al. 1998).

definition: A tool that turns down resonances only while the sound is harsh.
note: Command form, consistent with harshness = Härte. 'De-Harsh' would be understood by analogy with 'De-Esser' but is not German; 'Entschärfen' is catchy but blurs Schärfe (sharpness). Not a De-Esser (which keys on level in one band).

definition: A tool that splits a sound into its transient part and its sustained part, to rebalance them.
note: Noun title built from the chosen single terms (Attack, Körper); 'Attack & Body' is the pure-loan title many sound designers would accept. Not 'Transient-Shaper' (works on level, not on a split).
alternatives: Attack & Body; Anschlag und Körper; Transiente und Körper

definition: A tool that separates a sound into layers and mixes them again at new levels.
note: 'Layer' is the sound-design word for sound layers (Layering) and keeps them apart from the 'Ebenen' of a look; 'Remix' is naturalised. 'Schichten neu mischen' is the loan-free command form.
alternatives: Schichten neu mischen; Layer neu mischen; Schichten-Remix

definition: A tool that turns the tension curve into gain and brightness automation.
note: Compact compound like 'Hüllkurvenformer'; drawback: engineers may read 'Spannung' as voltage. 'Spannungsbogen formen' is more idiomatic (Spannungsbogen = dramatic arc) but is a command, not a title.

definition: A tool that finds and crossfades loop points where the sound repeats best.
note: 'Loop-Finder' names the main job and reads as German ('Finder' is native); 'Loop-Maker' is the plain loan; 'Loop-Generator' collides with 'Generator' (the Workbench sound generator).

definition: Several slightly different versions of one sound, to avoid repetition in games.
note: German game-audio usage; 'Varianten' also common.

definition: A tool that repairs what the quality checks flag before a sound is exported.
note: Noun title as in the English.

definition: Reverberation fed only from the decays of the events, keeping the attacks dry.
note: Follows the studio idiom 'Hall auf die Snare'; 'Hall im Ausklang' is smoother and shorter but loses the per-event plural. 'Hall' (not 'Reverb') is standard German studio usage.

definition: Saturation applied only to the events' attacks or bodies.
note: 'anzerren' is the studio verb for driving lightly into distortion; 'Hits' is common in German sound design ('Impacts & Hits'). 'Schläge' is more German but evokes blows; 'Ereignisse sättigen' is exact but flat.
alternatives: Schläge anzerren; Ereignisse sättigen; Drive the Hits

definition: A tool that lengthens or shortens how long each event rings after its peak.
note: 'nachklingen' carries 'ring'; 'Ausschwingzeit' is acoustically correct but easily confused with Abklingzeit (T60).

definition: A tool that evens out how loud the events are, one gain per event, without touching their shape.
note: Command form (object + infinitive, Microsoft German style). 'angleichen' stresses the result (equal loudness), 'ausgleichen' the process. Not 'komprimieren' (a compressor changes the shape).
alternatives: Ereignispegel angleichen; Ereignisse ausgleichen; Level the Events

definition: Turn stereo into mono with the channels' phase lined up, so nothing cancels.
note: A literal 'falten' is avoided because 'Faltung' is German for convolution. 'phasenrichtig' marks the difference from a plain 'auf Mono summieren' (sum to mono); 'zusammenführen' is shorter but hides the point.
alternatives: Auf Mono zusammenführen; Phasenrichtig zu Mono; Fold to Mono

definition: Make or widen stereo only after the attacks, keeping attacks centred and the result mono-compatible.
note: Command form; 'verbreitern' as in 'Stereobreite'. 'aufweiten' is also heard in studios.
alternatives: Ausklänge aufweiten; Stereo im Ausklang; Widen the Tails

definition: Turn more channels into fewer.
note: Broadcast and surround usage; Audacity de 'heruntermischen'.

definition: How well a stereo sound survives being summed to mono.
Making two signals less alike while keeping their spectrum, to widen a stereo image.
Regular notches in a spectrum when a signal is summed with a delayed copy of itself.
Loss of level when signals of opposite phase are summed.
A faint smear of a sound before its attack, caused by frame-based processing.
note: German codec literature (MP3/AAC): Vorecho.

definition: An equaliser: a filter that changes the level of frequency bands.
note: 'Entzerrer' is the older broadcast term. 'das Filter' in technical prose, 'der Filter' in studio speech.

definition: An EQ whose band gains follow the level in each band.
Parameter changes over time, recorded or drawn.
note: Cubase, Logic and Ableton de say 'Automation'; 'Automatisierung' is general IT German.

definition: A processor that turns loud passages down by a ratio above a threshold.
The level above which a processor acts.
note: Control label in German DAWs (Cubase, Logic); German textbooks: 'Threshold (Arbeitspunkt, Schwellwert)' (HdM Stuttgart, Regelverstärker). 'Schwellenwert' reads well in running text.

definition: How strongly a compressor turns the level down above its threshold.
note: HdM Stuttgart: 'Ratio (Kompressionsstärke)'; Audacity de 'Verhältnis'.

definition: How fast a processor reacts when the level rises.
note: HdM Stuttgart: 'Attack-Time (Ansprechzeit)'. Control label simply 'Attack'.

definition: How fast a processor recovers when the level falls.
note: HdM Stuttgart: 'Release-Time (Rücklaufzeit)'. Control label simply 'Release'.

definition: A processor or condition that opens only above a threshold.
note: As a processor also 'Rauschsperre' (Noise Gate); in loudness metering 'Gate/Gating' (ZDF Vorgaben 2022: 'Absolutes Gate −70 LUFS').

definition: Soft distortion that adds harmonics and rounds peaks.
Audible rise and fall of the background caused by a compressor.
note: HdM Stuttgart: '„Pumpen“ eines Kompressors'.

definition: How alike the events are in loudness.
note: CH: Gleichmässigkeit.

definition: Effects applied one after another to a sound.
A saved set of settings.
A gradual blend from one sound into another.
note: German uses the noun 'Morphing' (verb 'morphen'); not 'Crossfade', which only blends levels.

definition: Combining the spectrum of one sound with the envelope or excitation of another.
note: excitation = Anregung (source-filter model), not 'Erregung' (= arousal).

definition: Filtering one sound by another, for example by a room's impulse response.
note: Faltungshall. This is why 'fold to mono' is not rendered with 'falten'.

definition: Giving one sound the level envelope of another.
Multiplying two signals, which creates sum and difference frequencies.
Built from many short grains of sound.
note: Granularsynthese; studio usage 'Grains'.

definition: A short added sound placed at a moment of another sound to emphasise it.
note: 'Akzent' is literal and familiar from music; 'Betonung' names the act rather than the added sound; 'Akzentsound' is unambiguous but longer.

definition: A part of the app that makes new sounds from parameters.
A sound generator built from oscillators, noise, envelopes and filters.
A physical model of a struck object of a given material and shape.
note: 'Impacts' is common in German sound design (library categories 'Impacts & Hits'); use 'Anschlagmodell' in docs when the model itself is meant.

definition: Rebuilding a sound from parameters measured on it, such as its partials and decays.
Made of resonant modes, each with a frequency and a decay.
note: Modalsynthese; die Mode, pl. Moden.

definition: A continuous sound made of many small events, such as rain, fire or gravel.
A generator in which an action, such as an object moving or a force, drives the sound of a medium that responds to it (gravel, water, air).
note: Literal and clear; echoes Newton's 'actio = reactio', which fits. 'Anregung und Antwort' is acoustically apt but collides with Anregung = excitation.
alternatives: Einwirkung und Reaktion; Anregung und Antwort; Action & Reaction

definition: What reacts to an action: gravel, leaves, water, air, sparks or a force field.
A curve that controls a sound's parameters over time.
note: 'Steuerkurve' (control curve) is precise and avoids the clash with drive = Anzerrung (drive the hits); 'Antriebskurve' is literal but sounds mechanical.

definition: How slowly a reaction settles after the action stops.
Everyday sounds performed and recorded in sync with picture.
note: German film-sound practice: Foley, Geräuschemacher(in). Capitalised as in English (after Jack Foley).

definition: The background sound of a place.
note: German film-sound and sound-design standard (die Atmo, pl. Atmos; Atmo-Aufnahme).

definition: A short sound played once, such as a hit or a UI click.
The sound of something moving fast past the listener.
note: SFX library usage; 'Wusch' is the German onomatopoeia.

definition: The last steps before export: format, channels, fades and level.
note: 'Feinschliff' is more idiomatic but suggests polish rather than format and channels.
Material: das Gummi (DE), der Gummi (AT, also DE colloquial).

definition: A long solid body, such as a rod or beam.
note: Not 'Takt' (musical bar).

definition: A thin flat body.
A stretched skin, as on a drum.
note: AT also 'Membrane'.

definition: A thin curved body, such as a can or pot.
A stiff string or wire that rings with slightly stretched (inharmonic) partials.
note: Literal 'Draht' keeps the object-like naming of the shape list; physically a tensioned string is modelled, so choose 'Saite' if non-metal strings are meant.

definition: A hollow body with flat sides.
A row of a DAW session that holds clips on the timeline and has its own mixer channel.
note: Cubase, Logic and Ableton de 'Spur'. Not 'Lane' (a band inside a strip) or 'Kanal' (one signal of a sound file).

definition: A track that holds other tracks: it sums their sound and can show them as one.
note: Cubase de 'Ordnerspur'; REAPER users say 'Ordner'; Logic de 'Spurstapel' (track stack). Playhead: 'Spuren in einem Ordner'.

definition: One piece of audio or MIDI on a track, placed at a point in time.
note: Ableton and Studio One de 'Clip'; Cubase 'Event', REAPER 'Item', Logic 'Region'. Here 'Ereignis' is a sound event and 'Region' a named span of time.

definition: All of one piece of DAW work: its tracks, clips, routing and settings; also called a project.
The time axis of a session, along which clips are placed.
A named point in time stored in a session or a sound file (a cue in a WAV file).
note: Not 'Markierung': 'Markierungen' are the marks Playhead draws on a strip.

definition: A named span of time with a start and an end, stored in a session or a sound file.
note: REAPER and WaveLab 'Region'. In Logic a Region is a clip.

definition: Making a clip or an edit jump to the nearest grid line, marker, clip edge or onset while it is moved.
note: Logic de 'Einrasten'. Playhead: 'An Onsets einrasten'.

definition: Silencing a track without removing it; the button is often labelled M.
note: Buttons 'Stumm' or M.

definition: Hearing only the soloed tracks; the button is often labelled S.
The level control of a mixer channel.
Where a sound sits between left and right; also the control that sets it.
note: Standard studio term (das Panorama; Panoramaregler). 'Pan' is also heard as a control label.

definition: A mixer channel that sums the signals sent to it, so they can be processed together (a drum bus, a reverb bus).
The bus everything is summed into before the output: what is rendered as the mix.
note: 'Summe' is classic German studio usage.

definition: A copy of a track's signal sent to a bus at its own level, while the track keeps playing.
An effect in a channel's own signal path, which all of the signal passes through.
How signals travel between tracks, buses, sends and outputs.
The sum of all tracks as it is heard; also the work of balancing them.
note: Playhead: 'Ordner-Mix'.

definition: A submix of related tracks (drums, dialogue, music) rendered to its own file, so the parts can be mixed or delivered separately.
note: Loan (der Stem, pl. Stems).

definition: A point where the waveform crosses zero; cuts and loop points made there do not click.
The distance in dB between the highest level a signal reaches and the level where it would clip.
note: Studio loan (der Headroom); 'Aussteuerungsreserve' in broadcast texts.

definition: The span in dB between a sound's loud and quiet parts, or between the highest level a system takes and its noise floor.
note: A level measure in dB; the loudness range (Lautheitsbereich, LRA) is a loudness measure in LU.

definition: How much the loudness of a programme varies, in LU: the span between the 10th and 95th percentile of its short-term loudness.
note: EBU Tech 3342; German broadcast usage, e.g. ZDF 2022 spec: 'Lautheitsbereich („Loudness Range“, LRA)'.

definition: The loudness of a whole programme, with silence and quiet passages gated out, in LUFS.
note: EBU R 128; 'Programmlautheit' in ARD/ZDF specifications.

definition: Loudness over a sliding 3 s window, in LUFS.
note: EBU Tech 3341.

definition: Loudness over a sliding 400 ms window, in LUFS.
note: EBU Tech 3341.

definition: The integrated loudness a programme is delivered or played at, such as −23 LUFS for EBU R 128 broadcast or about −14 LUFS on streaming services.
Bringing two versions to the same loudness before comparing them, so that the louder one does not seem better only because it is louder.
note: As in Playhead ('Lautheit angleichen').

definition: Switching between two versions, ideally at matched loudness, to hear which is better.
A finished recording played for comparison while mixing or mastering.
The ratio of peak to RMS level, in dB: high for punchy, dynamic sound, low for dense, compressed sound.
note: 'Scheitelfaktor' in electrical engineering (DIN).

definition: The root mean square of a signal over a window: its average power, as a level.
How different the two channels are, from mono (not at all) to wide.
How a quantity, usually level, changes over the course of a sound; also a drawn curve that controls a parameter.
note: Standard German (die Hüllkurve), as in all German synths and DAWs; level envelope = Pegelhüllkurve (envelope transfer).

definition: A range of frequencies measured or processed together: an EQ band, a critical band, a mel band.
note: A critical band is a Frequenzgruppe (this vocabulary).

definition: A filter that passes the frequencies above its cutoff and attenuates those below.
A filter that passes the frequencies below its cutoff and attenuates those above.
A compressor with a very high ratio and a fast attack that keeps the level below a ceiling.
A compressor that works on several frequency bands separately.
A processor that raises or lowers the attack and the sustain of sounds independently of their level.
note: 'Transient Designer' (SPL) became the generic German studio word.

definition: A second input through which another signal controls a processor, as when music is turned down under dialogue.
Turning one sound down automatically while another plays, usually with a sidechained compressor.
The dense reflections of a sound in a space, or an effect that imitates them.
note: As in reverb on the tails = Hall auf die Ausklänge.

definition: An effect that plays the sound again after a set time, often repeating and fading (echo).
Low-level noise added when the bit depth is reduced, so that the rounding error becomes noise instead of distortion.
The last stage before release: the final EQ, dynamics and loudness of a mix, and checks for the delivery format.
The moment in a dance track when the full beat and bass come in, usually after a build-up or a breakdown.
note: Playhead never uses 'Drop' for a fall in level.

definition: A passage that raises tension towards a drop: rising pitch, filter sweeps, faster rolls, a riser.
A passage where the beat and bass fall away, leaving pads, chords or vocals.
A sound that rises in pitch, brightness or level to lead into a drop or a transition.
note: Sound-design and EDM loan (der Riser); no established German word.

definition: A glide through a range of frequencies: a tone or noise whose pitch or brightness moves, or a filter swept across the spectrum.
note: Loan (der Sweep); the measurement sense is 'Gleitsinus'.

definition: A stored position in a track that a DJ or a player jumps to or starts from.
The beats and bars of a track as a grid, used to sync, loop and jump in time.
note: As in German DJ software and Playhead; 'Beat-Raster' in running text where a German word reads better.

definition: Bringing two tracks to the same tempo with their beats aligned.
A run of bars, usually 8, 16 or 32 in dance music, that forms one musical unit; DJs mix at phrase boundaries.
The tonal centre and scale of a piece, such as A minor; DJs mix tracks in compatible keys (harmonic mixing).
